method: Native temporal stills, enlarged source/mask/peak-dim crops, actual decoded 720p full-composition frames and matching V4/V5 encoded detail comparison at twelve seconds
observations: Initial aperture coverage left strips at the top/bottom of some panes; the complete perspective apertures were expanded against source detail.
Source warm-colour gating missed white lamp cores; a separate bright-core gate was added and the five observed failures now have full coverage.
Initial sky sampling carried rock fragments; corrected sky segmentation was inspected against the photographed silhouettes.
Conservative scanline texture extension smeared real cloud detail into stripes; rejected and replaced with two-dimensional atmospheric extension.
Equal continuously crossfaded fields repeated at thirty seconds and could hover around the same texture position; replaced with sustained forward travel and brief phase renewal.
Far and middle mist have separate flow speed and ridgeline occlusion. Foreground utility mast details are excluded.
Latest unamplified full-composition and enlarged temporal stills retain photographed building, rail and rock structure. Playback quality remains for user review.
Decoded comparison inspected: left V4 and right V5 have matching time, crop and scale with readable labels; window cores dim with their panes and mist has broader broken coverage.

The initial lossy encoding introduced a small loop brightness step despite continuous source frames. The delivered QP0 minute passes regional/quiet-neighbour seams and six exact native-to-decoded YUV controls.
limitations: Cloud phase renewal is a procedural crossfade and can soften or double cloud detail briefly.
Mist is a two-dimensional optical approximation, not simulated volumetric fluid.
Numerical checks and still inspection do not establish a drastic perceptual improvement.
